title: Critical AI capability, active exploitation and control evidence now meet in one operating test
mainJudgement: The test is simple: when a warning lands, can the firm turn it into a clear, evidenced decision?

committeeQuestion.question: For the risks we say are critical—agentic AI, exploited vulnerabilities, sanctions change and data failure—can management show the trigger, intervention authority, evidence of action and closure decision?
committeeQuestion.why: This week’s signals are different in form but identical in management demand: speed matters only when the firm can recognise the trigger, act within authority and preserve a decision trail that survives challenge.
committeeQuestion.evidence: Ask for one recent end-to-end example: the alert or evaluation, named owner, authority to intervene, control action, exception decision, recovery or remediation proof, and dated closure record.

judgement.observation: This week’s AI, cyber, sanctions and data events all point to one management test: when a warning lands, can the firm turn it into a clear, evidenced decision?
judgement.executiveJudgement: The weakness is rarely seeing the alert. It is being able to show who could act, what they decided and whether the issue was closed properly. A policy or dashboard alone cannot do that.
judgement.implication: Pick two critical scenarios and trace the evidence from trigger to closure. Start with an exploited vulnerability and a sanctions change. Name the owner, their authority, the action taken and the proof it worked.
